content.text:
Federal loan limits for a period starting 2026-09-01 (P.L. 119-21 limits (periods of instruction beginning on or after July 1, 2026)): graduate unsubsidized $20,500.00 a year; professional unsubsidized $50,000.00 a year; Parent PLUS $20,000.00 a year and $65,000.00 total per student; dependent undergraduate $5,500.00/$6,500.00/$7,500.00 by year; independent undergraduate $9,500.00/$10,500.00/$12,500.00 by year; lifetime cap $257,500.00 (excluding Parent PLUS). Students enrolled with a loan on June 30, 2026 keep the old limits for up to 3 academic years.

General information, not financial or legal advice. Your servicer computes the official payment from your certified income and loan records. Use the StudentAid.gov Loan Simulator to confirm.

structuredContent.rules_in_force: P.L. 119-21 limits (periods of instruction beginning on or after July 1, 2026)

dependent_undergraduate.note: Excludes dependent students whose parents cannot get a Direct PLUS Loan; those students get the independent limits. Not changed by P.L. 119-21.
dependent_undergraduate.less_than_full_time: Annual limit reduced in direct proportion to less-than-full-time enrollment (rounded to the nearest whole percentage point), per a schedule the Secretary publishes.

independent_undergraduate.note: Also applies to dependent undergraduates whose parents cannot get a Direct PLUS Loan. Not changed by P.L. 119-21.
independent_undergraduate.less_than_full_time: Annual limit reduced in direct proportion to less-than-full-time enrollment, per the Secretary's schedule.

graduate.grad_plus: Not available. Graduate PLUS ended for periods of instruction beginning on or after July 1, 2026 (interim exception below).
graduate.aggregate_note: If the student is or has been a professional student, the graduate aggregate is $200,000 minus what was borrowed for professional study.
graduate.definition: Graduate student: program that awards a graduate credential other than a professional degree.

professional.grad_plus: Not available from July 1, 2026 (interim exception below).
professional.aggregate_note: If the student is or has been a graduate (non-professional) student, the professional aggregate is $200,000 minus what was borrowed for graduate study.
professional.definition: Professional student: program that awards a professional degree as defined in 34 CFR 668.2 as in effect on July 4, 2025.

parent_plus.aggregate_note: Counted without regard to amounts repaid, forgiven or discharged.
parent_plus.less_than_full_time: Per FSA's FAQ, Parent PLUS is not reduced for less-than-full-time enrollment.
parent_plus.repayment: Parent PLUS loans made on or after July 1, 2026 can be repaid only under the Tiered Standard plan; they cannot use RAP.

lifetime_limit_all_student_loans.note: Lifetime maximum for loans a student borrows under Title IV (undergraduate, graduate and professional, Direct and FFEL), not counting Parent PLUS loans borrowed for a dependent. Counted without regard to amounts repaid, forgiven or discharged.

structuredContent.institution_may_set_lower_limits: From July 1, 2026 a school may set lower annual loan limits for a program, applied the same way to all students in that program.
structuredContent.interim_exception: A student who on June 30, 2026 was enrolled in a program and had received a Direct Loan for it (or whose parent had) keeps the old limits, including Grad PLUS and uncapped Parent PLUS, for the expected time to credential: the lesser of 3 academic years or the time left in the program.
structuredContent.regulation_note: Loan limits come straight from HEA sec. 455(a)(3)-(8) as amended by P.L. 119-21 sec. 81001. The proration schedule for less-than-full-time study and the professional-degree list are set by the Department; check your school's financial aid office.
